name: Log Shattering / Projected Distinguishing Range (logarithmic)
details: For every finite binary class with positive projected distinguishing range, $\log_2|\operatorname{sh}(\mathcal H)|\geq\log_2\mathrm R^p(\mathcal H)$; more precisely it is at least $\log_2(\mathrm R^p(\mathcal H)+1)$.
proof: Choose a projection $\mathcal G=\mathcal H_{|S}$ attaining $r=\mathrm R^p(\mathcal H)$, and a minimum distinguishing coordinate set $T$ for $\mathcal G$.  Every coordinate in $T$ is active in $\mathcal G$, since an inactive coordinate could be deleted without changing any trace.  Hence it is active in $\mathcal H$, and its singleton is shattered by $\mathcal H$.  The $r$ distinct singleton sets in $T$, together with the empty set, give at least $r+1$ shattered subsets of $\mathcal H$.
witness_verification: For the trivial class $\mathcal T_n=\{\emptyset,[n]\}$, log shattering is $\log_2(n+1)$ while projected distinguishing range is $1$; hence no reverse affine-linear bound holds.
